rv.q: At root, such solo endeavours evince the potency of storytelling and there were few better storytellers than Charles Dickens, who brought his own page-turners to the stage in rapturously received renditions.
Now we find Izzard doing a spellbinding solo turn in Charles Dickens's saga of self-discovery, Great Expectations.
What she certainly proves here is her unparalleled, really rather sublime, storytelling chops.
Izzard does herself, and Dickens, proud.
Eddie Izzard’s solo offering is a welcome but surprisingly staid addition to the canon, offering a loving, detailed take on Dickens’s most lovable novel.
Mostly, though, the frantic skip through the story comes at the expense of depth.
If you’re a neutral, as I am, be warned that it’s an evening which has its longueurs as well as its charms.
Izzard’s jokey voices and the precise, comical gestures she uses to invoke a place or person seem at war with the text rather than in service to it.
This is very special, and surely a must-see for Eddie Izzard fans and Charles Dickens enthusiasts.
The craft, and the emotion it provokes, is more than enough in compensation.
